title: Choose the look for the Dapper website
question: The roll dealt the Road-Test Feature. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. (The scroll-frame car section stays; this sets everything around it.)

options.label: Road-Test Feature
options.thesis: Every page is a road-test feature: full-bleed car photography, a hard-ruled spec box, and a verdict.
options.viewport: A red DAPPER masthead across the top, the car photo full-bleed under it, cover lines on the left as the navigation, and a spec box on the right holding the service rows and Book an appointment.
options.risk: Can tip into editorial cliché if the photography is weak or the type is set timidly.

raised.raise: Every figure (step number, tint %, price) is set as a fixed readout in one engineered digit form, never as loose body text.
One strict column grid; every rule, photo and spec box snaps to it, like a printed page.
The ten vehicle types become a browsable rack of full-height covers, not a list of links.
The portfolio reads as editions of one car: the same subject pulled before and after, side by side.

options.label: The 50/50 Tape Line
options.lineage: the paint-correction test panel: tape down the middle, half corrected
options.thesis: The detailer's own proof ritual: a strip of masking tape splits every view into before and after.
options.viewport: One car split by a vertical tape strip; the left half hazy and swirled, the right half mirror-gloss. The navigation is written on the tape, with Book a bay in red.
options.risk: Before/after sliders are familiar on detailing sites; it lands only if the tape owns the whole system, not just one slider.

options.label: Tint Wall
options.thesis: The site is a wall of glass panes; picking a service floods its pane, and tint shades run 70% to 5%.
options.viewport: A glazing grid filling the screen: one big photo pane with the headline, service panes, a red Book pane, and a row of tint panes from light to dark.
options.case: Fuses strongly with window tint and glass; holds on clarity, loses on whether car owners see themselves in it.
options.risk: Can read as architecture rather than cars.

options.label: Build Sheet
options.thesis: The process as numbered build steps: each step brings one new treatment in red while earlier work ghosts back.
options.viewport: A huge step numeral, the car ghosted with the new treatment outlined in red, a 1:1 call-out box, and the six steps along the bottom.
options.case: Makes the process crystal clear; loses on audience identification and the dark Dapper mood.
options.risk: Sky-blue ground moves away from the dark Dapper identity.

options.label: Nixie Counter
options.risk: Detailing customers do not see themselves in lab equipment.

options.label: ANSI Nightboard
options.viewport: A title screen in block art.
options.kept: A strict grid everything snaps to.

options.label: Deck Wall
options.kept: Vehicle types as a rack of full-height covers.

options.label: Silkscreen Loft
options.risk: Reads as art gallery, not a garage.
options.kept: Portfolio as before/after editions of one car.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Premium dark automotive: full-bleed car photo, big white headline, red pill button.
canonCard.viewport: Car photo, left-aligned headline, one red Book button.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other detailing studio's site.
